text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it actually does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: you move things to better places, but you don’t throw away your belongings. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand for anyone who works on it later, including yourself. Over time, messy code builds up what programmers call "technical debt." This means that quick, careless fixes now will cost you more time and effort to fix in the future. By refactoring regularly, you pay off that debt, keeping your software healthy, flexible, and much simpler to maintain.
